This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation .
SCCH 5 2.

The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 11.06.2019 at about 4.00 p.m. while riding his motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA53EZ8283 slowly and cautiously on Kammanahalli Min Road,
Ullasappa Circle, Bengaluru, a car bearing Reg.No.KA05AB1060 came in high speed rash and negligently caused accident, out of the said accident, he sustained grievous injuries, so that, he was immediately taken to Specialist Hospital, after first aid shifted to Kodagu Institute of Medical Science and Hospital, wherein he has taken treatment as indoor patient, surgery is conducted, spent medical expenses of Rs.2,00,000/.
3.

entities.text: Kodagu Institute of Medical Science and Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, working as salesman, thereby earning Rs.15,000/
p.m.

due to this accident he has lost his service and income, he is unable to do anything, out of this accident crime SCCH 5 No.67/2019 is registered against the said car and its driver before the Banasawadi Traffic Police.
R1 is the insurer, R2 is owner of the said car, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.15,00,000/ with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
4.

On service of notice, respondent No.1/insurer has appeared and filed written statement denying entire case of the petitioner, further stated that petitioner has to prove all his allegations, strictly there is no compliance of Sec.158(6) and 134(c) of M.V.Act, petitioner has to prove his age and income, petitioner had no driving license at the time of accident, further he is entitled to take shelter under Sec.147 and 149(2) of M.V.Act, claim made by the petitioner is higher side, hence petition is SCCH 5 not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On service of notice, R2/owner has appeared and filed written statement denying entire case of the petitioner, further stated that, his driver had all the relevant documents at the time of accident,
insurance policy issued by R1 bearing No.0725813118P108746384 is valid since 05.10.2018 to 04.10.2019, R1 has to indemnify the same, petitioner has to prove all the allegations made by him,

6. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
SCCH 5 ::ISSUES::
1. Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 11.06.2019 at about 4.00 p.m. near Kammanahalli Main Road, Ullasappa Circle, Bengaluru due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Reg.No.KA05AB1060 by its driver, as mentioned in claim petition?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
7. In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW1, examined 2 witnesses as PW2 and PW3 and marked 16 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, FDA, RTO Rajajinagara has deposed his evidence as SCCH 5 RW1 and marked 4 documents as per Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.4 and closed his evidence.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
9. Issue No.1: As per case of the petitioner, very accident is occurred on the alleged place, date and time due to negligency of driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA 05AB1060.

In their written statement, R1 and R2 have not denied place, date and time of the accident, they have denied negligency of the car driver, to prove the said facts SCCH 5 they have not produced any evidence and not furnished any documents.

10. To prove negligency of the car driver, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW1 and furnished copy of FIR marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint marked as Ex.P.2, copy of sketch marked as Ex.P.3, copy of mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of IMV Report marked as Ex.P.5, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.7.
In crossexamination also sdeposed that, there is negligency of the car driver.

3 11.

sentences.text:
The police papers marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.7 speaks that, case is only against car and its driver,
which supports the version of the petitioner.

12. On the other hand, FDA, RTO Rajajinagar has deposed his evidence as RW1 about only fitness of the SCCH 5 car and not about other aspects, it reveals that, there is sufficient evidence on record to hold that, very accident is occurred due to negligecy of the car driver, but not by the petitioner, so that, considering the same, I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2: As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained fracture distal end radius right, head injury (acute EDH with undisplaced fracture of right parietal bone with hematoma),
multiple lacerated wound.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.7.
14.

Further Medical Record Technician at Specialist Hospital has deposed his evidence as PW2 and furnished authorization letter marked as Ex.P.9, case sheet marked as Ex.P.10, copy of Police Intimation memo marked as Ex.P.11, copy of MLC Extract marked SCCH 5 as Ex.P.12, Xray Films marked as Ex.P.13 and CTScan marked as Ex.P.14.
15.

Further Dr.Chidanand K.J.C. Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics has been examined as PW3 and furnished clinical notes marked as Ex.P.15, Xray Films marked as Ex.P.16 and he has assessed physical disability from right upper limb and to whole body is 10.33%.
16.

entities.text: Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Petitioner has taken first aid at Specialist hospital and surgery is conducted in Government Hospital Wenlock, Mangalore Kodagu Institute of Medical Science and NIMHANS.
In this regard there are no documents on record.

Ex.P.10 case sheet of the Specialist Hospital, Bengaluru and on persal of the same, he is admitted in the said hospital on 11.06.2019 and discharged on same day,
there is no surgery, but as per SCCH 5 the case of the petitioner surgery is conducted at Government Hospital Wenlock, Mangalore Kodagu Institute of Medical Science and NIMHANS and underwent craniotomy and evacuation of hematoma, but to that extent there are no oral or documentary evidence.

entities.text: Mangalore Kodagu Institute of Medical Science and NIMHANS
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As per the evidence of the Doctor, there is only a conservative treatment, there is no surgery.
Further this Doctor has not treated the petitioner, even he has not gone through the case history, said fact is admitted in crossexamination.
Further he has not issued any disability certificate.

As per the version of the Doctor, there is disability to the particular right upper limb at the rate of 10.33%, there was only conservative treatment, it reveals that, evidence of Doctor is exaggerative in manner, however fracture is admitted and conservative treatment is taken.

SCCH 5 17. Petitioner is working as Salesman at Metro Bar & Restaurant, aged about 25 years, considering all these aspects, disability to the particular limb is considered at the rate of 15%, after converting to the whole body, disability is considered at the rate of 5%, for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

sentences.text: As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 25 years, for proof of his age, he has not produced any documents, but on perusal of copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.7, age of the petitioner is mentioned as 22 years, accordingly relying on Ex.P.7 his age is considered about 22 to 25 years as on the date of accident
, hence multiplier 18 is applicable with reference to Sarla Verma case.
19. As per his case, he was working as Salesman, thereby earning Rs.15,000/ p.m. to prove the said fact, SCCH 5 there are no documents on record.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.14,000/ p.m.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Keeping in mind injuries caused to the petitioner, treatment taken, expenses incurred and also the pain suffered, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, it is just and necessary to allot compensation under other heads, accordingly for pain and sufferings compensation of Rs.15,000/
is awarded, for conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges Rs.15,000/ is SCCH 5 awarded,
for loss of amenities of life Rs.15,000/ is awarded, further he is entitled for Rs.14,000/ towards loss of income during laid up period.

Further petitioner is also entitled for compensation for medical expenses incurred by him, for which, he has produced medical bills marked as Ex.P.8 for an amount of Rs.84,356/.
21.

Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below: Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Loss of future income 1,51,20000 2.
Pain and sufferings 15,00000 3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,00000 attendant charges 4.
Medical Expenses 84,35600 5.
Loss of amenities in life 15,00000 6.
Loss of income during laid up 14,00000 period Total 2,94,55600 SCCH 5 22.
Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,94,556/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

23. In the case on hand, respondent No.1 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.0725813118P108746384, which is valid for the period from 05.10.2018 to 04.10.2019, the alleged accident was occurred on 11.06.2019, it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance Sri. 5 policy was in force.

sentences.text: Further driver of the car had driving licence at the time of the accident, hence naturally liability of R2 shall go against R1, so that, R1/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
SCCH 5 24. Issue No.3:

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,94,556/ (Rupees Two Lakhs Ninety Four Thousand Five Hundred Fifty Six Only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through epayment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
SCCH 5 The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.

2023)
